narrative:
The model estimated a 79.3% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That high risk estimate is why your law school application was denied; it does not mean failure is certain, but it means the school judged the predicted risk too high to admit you on this record.

The strongest reason was your third-year class standing: being in the lowest tenth was well below the average accepted student, around the sixth tenth, and it pushed the prediction most strongly toward bar failure. Your first-year standing was the second-strongest factor; also being in the lowest tenth, far below the accepted average near the sixth tenth, it added further risk. Your upper-middle family income, a common bracket among accepted students, was the third most influential factor, and it worked in your favor, slightly pushing toward passing, but it was not enough to outweigh the two academic signals.

To improve a future application, focus on evidence that you can handle rigorous law study and bar preparation: consider additional academic coursework or a graduate program, take structured test preparation and retake the admissions test if you can improve your score, and seek admissions advice about explaining your early academic record and demonstrating a stronger recent trajectory.
